text:
mira: Hey team, ran into a weird one in a notebook — importing AsyncClient seems to create background tasks that survive kernel restart / throw warnings. Minimal repro below.

sam: can you paste the warnings and a minimal snippet?

mira: sure, here's what I did:

```python
# notebook cell 1
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # no await, just import/construct

# later cell (async context, e.g. jupyter with nest_asyncio)
await client.generate('hello')
```

And after rerunning the kernel a few times I get: 

``nRuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncClient._token_refresher' was never awaited
Task was destroyed but it is pending!
Exception in callback Task._wakeup()
RuntimeError: Task got Future attached to a different loop
``

lina: ugh. I've seen "Task got Future attached to a different loop" when code schedules tasks on import before the running loop is set in notebooks.

sam: do you create an asyncio.create_task in __init__? that's the usual suspect.

mira: yep looks like the client starts a background token refresher on construction. Works fine in most servers, but notebooks + fast kernel restarts cause orphan tasks and confusing warnings.

sam: workaround for now: instantiate the client inside an async context or call a start method after the loop is running. e.g.

```python
# recommended workaround
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
await client.start()  # or use async with AsyncClient():
await client.generate('...')
await client.close()
```

mira: thanks. Could we make that the official pattern or make client lazy-start so import/construct is safe in sync contexts? Onboarding docs for notebooks would help too.

tj: assigning to eng-runtime to look into. Short term: docs + note in quickstart. Long term: I think we should avoid scheduling tasks in __init__ and instead start them in __aenter__ / start().

lina: agreed. Also add a clear error if user calls async methods before start so they get a helpful message instead of cryptic warnings.

sam: creating a small PR with two changes: (1) remove create_task from __init__ and add _ensure_started() that runs on first async call, (2) add Client.start() / Client.close() for explicit lifecycle. I can draft it.

mira: amazing, thanks. If you want a quick test matrix: normal uvicorn app, pytest+asyncio, and jupyter lab with nest_asyncio. The notebook case is the failing one for me.

dev-bot: Ticket created: RNW-1217 "AsyncClient: postpone background task creation to start()/__aenter__" (assign: tj)

tj: PR opened at https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1890 — lightweight change + tests for notebooks. Can folks review?

lina: reviewing now. small nit: add doc note to quickstart and a changelog entry.

sam: reviewed, added a unit test that simulates no running loop and ensures no create_task on init.

mira: verified on my notebook after installing the PR build — warnings gone, notebook flows are clean. :tada:

tj: merging shortly. I'll add a release note and backport to the 0.16.x branch.

mira: thanks all! saved me from multiple kernel resets.

sam: great catch — notebook DX matters.
